newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook- LME metals stumble with first step.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook- LME metals stumble with first step.

text.p: The base metals complex started off the week on its knees on Monday as flagship copper tested the low end of its range and nickel sank to five-month lows.
Copper has been in an indecisive mood in recent days, with seriously overbought technicals countering persistent speculative buying, analysts said.
Dwindling LME stocks had contributed to a bullish mood last week that saw prices climb steadily to hit a fresh one-year high of $2,548.
But on the charts copper has been looking tired and overheated and a period of consolidation or a downward correction was on the cards, analysts said.
A glaring sign of its overbought status was the presence of the 14-day RSI above the key 70 level for two weeks running.
"Most of the metals, especially copper, have been rising for some time without a correction. Maybe this is the correction everyone's been waiting for," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.
Support crumbled at the psychological $2,500 level during inter-office trading, but it may emerge then around $2,460, analysts said.

The correction may be brief as players will be unwilling to short the market with stocks low, especially considering recent concern about potential supply disruptions in South America, some analysts said.
On the upside, the next key resistance levels are at $2,550 and then $2,570, chartists said.
The biggest loser in the base metals line-up is volatile nickel, which tumbled to its lowest level since January on Monday morning after speculative selling triggered sell-stops.
Selling said to have been started by a large U.S. investment bank set off a downward spiral in nickel prices last week.
Losses intensified on Friday after mildly supportive concerns over a possible strike at producer Inco Ltd's Sudbury operations were lifted when the union reached a tentative contract deal.
"It was always looking to be sold down if an agreement was reached because people had taken precautionary hedging positions which would be liquidated," Bhar said.
"On top of that speculative players took the opportunity to trigger stops."
Nickel sank through recent support at $7,110, where it double-bottomed on April 14 and January 29, and was hovering just below the $7,000 area in inter-office trading.
Further down, support was expected at $6,940.
In other metals, aluminium was also vulnerable to the downside after stubborn resistance around the $1,640/$1,650 proved impossible to hurdle last week. But it was finding some support above $1,600.
Tin was also on shaky territory after sliding to below $5,600, the lowest in more than two years.
Zinc looked to take a breather from its upward climb for fresh 4-1/2 year highs and indulge in a corrective pull-back.
